Subject: Request: temporary SLO tolerance for Alpha Embedder rollout

Hi Nick,

Thanks again for partnering with us on the Alpha Embedder. As you begin routing a small percentage of AtlasAI traffic to the new encoder, we want to be transparent about expected performance during the staging window and propose a short-term SLO tolerance to cover initial ramp and warm-up behavior.

Proposal (summary):
- Duration: up to 45 days from first production traffic
- Latency SLO: temporary target of p95 <= 300ms (normal p95 target 150ms)
- Availability SLO: temporary target 99.5% uptime (normal 99.95%)
- Coverage: applies to up to 5% of requests routed to the Alpha Embedder

We will instrument additional telemetry and provide a daily digest during the pilot. If we observe regressions beyond those thresholds we will roll traffic back and notify you immediately.

Attached is a short addendum draft that formalizes this tolerance so your legal/procurement team can review. Can you confirm whether those parameters are sufficient for AtlasAI to proceed with the initial ramp?

Thanks,

--
Soojin Lee

Soojin —

Thanks for the context. Operational notes and proposal:

- Coverage measurement: per-request basis (we'll tag requests routed to the Alpha variant). This is the simplest and lowest-risk measurement to implement for a staged rollout.
- Duration: recommend 45 days. First 7–10 days are the highest risk (KV cache cold-starts + compilation/quantization warm paths). Extending to 45 days gives us a buffer for follow-up tuning.
- Latency expectation: p95 can spike to ~400–600ms during the first 24–48 hours for worst-case long-tail requests; a p95 <=300ms target is reasonable after the initial warm window. We propose a staged SLO: 0–48h: informational (no credit) but immediate rollback if errors >2%; day 3–7: p95 <=450ms (soft), day 8–45: p95 <=300ms (temporary).
- Availability: we can support temporary 99.5% uptime for the covered requests. If availability falls below 99% at any point we will trigger automatic rollback for the affected route and notify AtlasAI within 15 minutes.
- Tracing/telemetry: we'll grant AtlasAI read-only access to a scoped telemetry dashboard and can push raw trace exports for any incident windows (subject to NDAs).
- Rollback: we can enact a route rollback within 5 minutes; on-call ops contact is me (dev.patel@redwoodinference.com) and our SRE rotation (sre-oncall@redwoodinference.com).

Caveats: autoscale cold-starts on certain GPU shapes can cause latency spikes until kernels are JIT'd; we should keep traffic at <=5% as proposed and introduce a ramp schedule (0.5% -> 1% -> 3% -> 5% over 48h) to reduce risk.

Happy to stand up a short runbook for AtlasAI's SREs.

- Dev

Soojin/Dev —

Legal/sales notes on the addendum:
- Include a 45-day limit (no automatic renewal).
- Add a rollback commitment (Redwood will revert routing in <=5 minutes upon availability <99%).
- Limit the tolerance to requests explicitly routed to the Alpha Embedder (per-request tagging).
- If availability dips below 99% for any 24h window during the tolerance period, AtlasAI is eligible for a service credit equal to 20% of that day's billed usage for the covered traffic — capped at the total charges for the tolerance period.
- Require AtlasAI to sign an addendum and a limited-tech NDA for trace exports.

I've attached a redlined version with the above language. If you want, I can seed the procurement thread with these bullets so their legal sees the exact phrasing.

- Laura

- Credits: if availability dips below 99% for any 24h window, AtlasAI will receive a service credit equal to 20% of that day's billed usage for the covered traffic (capped as described in the addendum).
